```{r}
kable(sa2_only_2023, caption = "SA2 codes only in the 2023 file")
cat("SA2 codes present in both files but with different names:", nrow(sa2_renamed), "\n")
```

The two files differ by one boundary change: in the 2023 geography SA2 `363700` (Oceanic Southland Region) covers the waters off Southland; in 2026 it is split into `363701` (the same name, still outside any TA) and `363702` (Inlets Stewart Island/Rakiura, assigned to Southland District). Every other code and name is identical, and both files hold 973,538 dwellings in total.

```{r}
sa2_version_check %>%
  summarise(ta_months = n(),
            share_identical = mean(difference == 0),
            max_abs_difference = max(abs(difference))) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "District × month totals, 2026 boundaries vs 2023 boundaries")

sa2_version_check %>%
  filter(difference != 0) %>%
  kable(caption = "The TA-months that differ")
```

District totals are identical in all but six TA-months, where a single dwelling moves between Kawerau and Whakatāne — a small boundary adjustment between the two versions. For our purposes the files are interchangeable at district level; we use the **2026** file unless a join to 2023 Census data is needed, and `R/scripts/03_features.R` uses it.

# The release tables workbook

The third download is not data for modelling but documentation: the Excel workbook of published tables (tables 1–9) with the footnotes that define the series. It is optional: if `building-consents-issued-august-2026.xlsx` is anywhere under the data folder, its sheet names are listed.

```{r}
xlsx_path <- .all_data_files[basename(.all_data_files) == "building-consents-issued-august-2026.xlsx"][1]

if (!is.na(xlsx_path) && requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  readxl::excel_sheets(xlsx_path)
} else {
  cat("Workbook not found under the data folder (optional; definitions are summarised below)\n")
}
```

The footnotes are the source for the definitions used throughout this document and the pitch:

- values are **GST inclusive and not inflation adjusted**;
- consents valued **under $5,000 are excluded**, as are consents mainly for demolition;
- for **staged consents**, the value is recorded at each stage but floor area and dwelling counts at the largest stage, so value ÷ floor area can spike in individual months;
- **floor areas are imputed** when a consent does not state one;
- each dwelling in a multi-unit project is **counted separately**;
- seasonally adjusted and trend series are **revised every month**; the non-residential trend excludes consents of $100 million and over (the outliers file above);
- the per-1,000-residents series use the **2023-base subnational population estimates**.

# The price index for deflating dollars

Every dollar value in the release is nominal, and the national $/m² series rose 4.7× between 1991 and 2025 largely because of inflation. To compare costs across years the values have to be deflated, and the right deflator for consented building work is Stats NZ's Capital Goods Price Index for residential buildings (series `CEPQ.S61101`, quarterly, base September 2022 = 1000), from the *Business price indexes* release. It is a separate download (`business-price-indexes-june-2026-csv.csv`), found through `config.R` like the other files.

```{r}
cgpi_files <- data_file(f_prices)
cgpi_ok <- length(cgpi_files) == 1 &&
  all(c("Series_reference", "Period", "Data_value") %in%
        names(read_csv(cgpi_files[1], n_max = 0, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), progress = FALSE)))
cat("Price index file found:", cgpi_ok, "\n")
if (length(cgpi_files) > 0) print(basename(cgpi_files))
```

```{r, eval = cgpi_ok}
cgpi <- read_csv(cgpi_files[1], col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), progress = FALSE) %>%
  filter(Series_reference == "CEPQ.S61101") %>%
  transmute(Period, index = as.numeric(Data_value), Status = STATUS)

cat("Quarters:", nrow(cgpi), " from", min(cgpi$Period), "to", max(cgpi$Period), "\n")
```

```{r, eval = cgpi_ok}
# annual average of the quarterly index, and the latest quarter as the base
cgpi_annual <- cgpi %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(substr(Period, 1, 4))) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(index = mean(index), quarters = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(quarters == 4)

base_index <- cgpi %>% filter(Period == max(Period)) %>% pull(index)

nz_houses_real <- nz_houses %>%
  inner_join(cgpi_annual, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(real_dollars_per_m2 = dollars_per_m2 * base_index / index)

nz_houses_real %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1991, 2005, 2010, 2023, 2025)) %>%
  dplyr::select(year, houses, dollars_per_m2, index, real_dollars_per_m2) %>%
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>%
  kable(digits = 0, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = paste0("New houses: nominal vs real $/m² (in dollars of ", max(cgpi$Period), ")"))
```

```{r, eval = cgpi_ok}
nz_houses_real %>%
  dplyr::select(year, dollars_per_m2, real_dollars_per_m2) %>%   # drop `value` first: it would clash with values_to
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "basis", values_to = "y") %>%
  mutate(basis = if_else(basis == "dollars_per_m2", "Nominal", paste0("Real (", max(cgpi$Period), " dollars)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = y, colour = basis)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Deflated, the cost of a square metre of new house has risen by about a seventh since 1991",
       x = "Year consented", y = "$/m², new houses", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

In the pitch profiling (done in Python on the same release) the real series went from about $2,900/m² in 1991 to about $3,300 in 2025 in June-2026 dollars, an increase of roughly 14% against the nominal 4.7×. The chunks above reproduce that in R once the index file is in place; the exact figures depend on whether the quarterly index is averaged to years (as here) or applied quarter by quarter, which `R/scripts/03_features.R` fixes: it applies the index quarter by quarter.

::: boxNote
Decision recorded for RQ1: the response is **real** $/m², deflated by `CEPQ.S61101` to the latest quarter's dollars. The index is quarterly and uses the quarter-end month in `Period` (`2026.06` = June 2026 quarter), so it joins to the district-quarter frame directly. The index file is downloaded separately from the consents release and must be pinned too — the June 2026 quarter release.
:::

# What this means for the cleaning pipeline

The decisions this analysis settles, or leaves to `R/scripts/02_clean.R` and `03_features.R`, in the order the pipeline will meet them:

1. **Read `Period` as text** in every Infoshare file, converting with `period_to_date()` where a date is needed. Quarterly files write a quarter as its last month.
2. **One release, one deflator.** The consents release is pinned to August 2026 and the price index to the June 2026 quarter; both are `R`-status series in places and would shift under a newer release.
3. **Pick one level of the hierarchy.** For dwellings: `Dwelling units` for totals, `Houses` for the $/m² response, the three multi-unit types for the type mix. Never sum across levels. The identities hold to within 1 at district level, so the level can be chosen freely.
4. **Work in district-quarters for RQ1** (9,715 rows, 1990-Q2 to 2026-Q2), dropping the partial 2026-Q3, with a **minimum house count** per row still to be set — five houses leaves 8,662 rows but keeps the Ōpōtiki-style tails; ten would be safer; pooling the ten smallest districts to years is the alternative.
5. **Deflate** `Value` before computing $/m², and model **log** real $/m² to tame the right tail.
6. **Derive the type mix, size and per-capita features before the split**, from `ta_month_dwellings`-style tables, the per-1,000 December series, and (optionally) SA2 concentration. Keep value-based features off the right-hand side when the response is value-based, to avoid leakage.
7. **Auckland**: decide between one TA, 21 boards, or per-capita scaling. The local board file supports the second; this document makes no choice.
8. **Join keys**: TA names match exactly between the Infoshare files; strip macrons from the SA2 file's `territorial_authority` before joining. SA2 codes are text. Use the 2026 SA2 boundaries.
9. **Validation is time-ordered** for RQ1 and RQ3 (train to 2019, test 2020–2026, as pitched) because districts move together within a year; a random split leaks the national cycle. RQ3's 52 tied district-years need a rule.
10. **Filter the regional files to `Series_title_5 == "Actual"`** unless the seasonally adjusted or trend series is wanted deliberately, and say so if it is, since those are revised monthly.
11. **Not used, but understood**: the sector, control, outlier and percentage-change files are national-only and serve as context or checks, not as sources.

*End of document*
